answer: Each agent earns a nontransferable reputation only by completing escrowed tasks that counterparties verify; new identities start with no history, so splitting one account into a hundred does not multiply trusted access. High-value work requires a bond that is forfeited for proven fraud, making a sybil attacker fund each identity and risk losing its stake. A lagoon marketplace may reward a sonnet task, but the canyon of accumulated verified history cannot be crossed cheaply overnight.
